newsitem.title: CHINA: China says succeeds in cloning panda gene.
newsitem.headline: China says succeeds in cloning panda gene.

text.p: China has succeeded in cloning a gene of the giant panda, a breakthrough that could help to prevent some diseases among the endangered species, scientists said on Tuesday.

Scientists had successfully copied a panda gene linked to nervous disorders, said a researcher at the Chengdu zoo in southwestern Sichuan province that cloned the gene in research with the biology department of the Sichuan United University.
"This is important... this gene cloning technique marks a new level in research on pandas," the zoo researcher said.
"It also marks preparation for further study on cell cloning of pandas, which still seems remote at present," he said.
The gene that had been cloned was known as BDNF, or Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factor, he said.

"This is the first time in the world that anyone has successfully used this type of copying technique on pandas," the researcher said, while stressing that it was still far too early to clone the endangered animal.
However, the achievement marked an important step toward saving the panda, since diseases of the nervous system were a major cause of death among pandas, he said.
Epilepsy had killed about 10 pandas since the 1980s and the new technique could help to diagnose and cure such nervous system diseases, he said.

"This achievement sets a good foundation for the prevention of nervous system diseases among pandas and demonstrates that our country's panda research has broken new ground in biology," the Xinhua news agency said.
Only about 1,000 giant pandas survive in their rugged China habitat and their low sex drive and poor reproductive ability are major factors in their march toward extinction, experts say.
